title: JWT algorithm confusion: the token's own header selects the verification algorithm
index_line: T-0011 · AUTH_DECISION · alg:none / RS256→HS256 confusion / kid injection · corroborated
invariant_violated: The app trusts the token's own header to select the verification algorithm and key; the header is attacker-controlled data.

mechanism.does: attacker controls the bearer token (captured or self-issued)
library reads the alg header before verification
bypass: alg:none variants, HS256 signed with the fetched public key, kid traversal/SQL/command, jku/x5u pointing at attacker JWKS
verification passes with an attacker-chosen key
forged claims accepted: sub/role/admin flipped to administrator

encoding.jwt.value: alg:none / None / NONE variants · HS256-with-public-key · kid:'../../../dev/null' · jku:http://attacker/jwks.json

guard.signature.value: the accepted-algorithms list — none must not be in it, RS256-only configs resist confusion

token.claims.value: sub:'1'|'administrator', role:'admin', admin:true, exp removed or far-future

preconditions.expr: public key or JWKS endpoint reachable (for confusion/jku variants)
token from request reaches the verify call
none — the attack targets the token path itself

success: forged alg:none token accepted — admin response returned
HS256 token signed with the public key verifies
kid:'../../../dev/null' token verifies with empty secret
claims reflected: role/sub visible in the response or subsequent API behaviour
failure_like: library rejects alg none (algorithms allowlist set)
RS256-only configuration rejects the confused HS256 token
false_positive: token merely DECODED for display without verification
custom middleware validates separately and catches the forgery

hazards: algorithm acceptance is a library-config fact per stack — inspect the actual options passed, not the docs' default
confusion needs the public key; jku/x5u make it attacker-supplied (SSRF-shaped, see T-0003)
non_transfers: opaque server-side sessions — no client-verifiable algorithm exists
